title: Stereochemistry
description: A molecule and its mirror image weigh the same, boil together and look the same to every test but one: polarised light turns one way through one and the other way through the other. Biot measured it in 1815 with sugar and turpentine, and a tube of solution still certifies a drug's purity. Rings have a hand of their own: cyclohexane folds into a chair, and a bulky group would rather sit out along the equator than up against the ring; the A value says by how much. Unlocks the Polarimeter.

puzzle.goal: A group sits equatorial or axial on a chair, the equatorial lower by A per mole. At temperature T, write the ratio K of equatorial to axial (Boltzmann).
puzzle.name: Conformer ratio
puzzle.ask: Find K for a phenyl group, A = 11700 J/mol, with R = 8.314 at T = @{T} K.
puzzle.method: ΔG = −RT ln K, with ΔG = −A from axial to equatorial.
